Simon — quick technical note on scope and assumptions for private/customer VPC installs (we'll also include this as vpc_shared_responsibility.txt):

- Deployment model: In customer-managed VPC deployments Redwood ships a private data plane runtime that runs in the customer's subnets (customer-owned EC2/GKE nodes or private subnet resources). The Redwood control plane remains in our hosted control plane (managed by Redwood) unless you opt for fully air-gapped Private package.
- Boundary assumption: Customer is responsible for network ACLs, VPC routing, and host OS patching for nodes they manage. Redwood is responsible for the application runtime hardening, container image supply chain, and in-process memory/KV cache isolation.
- Cloud provider: The pen test we referenced covers our application surfaces — it does not include validation of underlying cloud provider hypervisor or managed DB service operational controls (those remain under provider responsibility). We explicitly note which findings require customer action when they affect customer-managed hosts or network configs.
- Marketplace/partner components: If you install additional third-party agents/marketplace services into the same subnet, those are explicitly out of Redwood's pen test scope unless included in a custom engagement.

I'll attach the shared responsibility text and a short table mapping typical findings to 'Redwood' vs 'Customer' remediation owners. If you need us to extend pen test scope to include your managed infra components, we can quote a scoped engagement.

Attachment: vpc_shared_responsibility.txt

-Kar
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

- P1: CVE-2025-XXXX (container runtime privilege escalation) — patched and validated in our staging runner on 2026-02-13; mitigation deployed to customer-managed data plane images with rollout starting 2026-02-16. Owner: Karthik.
